questions.answer: There is no single store. Three routes are supported: (1) vendor connectors in Claude's connector directory, where you pay the vendor for the underlying service (for example a Timesheet Pro plan or a QuickBooks subscription); (2) marketplaces such as MCPize (subscribe per server with one API key and one invoice) and Apify's hosted MCP at https://mcp.apify.com (usage-based Actor runs billed to your Apify account); (3) individual paid servers, which typically show a Stripe checkout link on the first paid tool call or take a licence key. I could not verify MCPize's accepted buyer payment methods.

recommended_servers.name: Claude connectors directory (vendor-backed connectors; you pay the vendor for the service; not a server)
MCPize marketplace (paid and free servers, one API key, consolidated invoice; buyer payment methods not documented; not a server)
Apify hosted MCP (https://mcp.apify.com; OAuth sign-in; Actor runs billed to your Apify account, pay-per-event)
Stripe-based paid MCP flow (first paid tool call returns a Stripe checkout link; experimental SDK, test-mode write-up)

caveats: Most first-search results are creator-side monetisation blog posts and vendor marketing, not buyer guides; I treat prices in them as unverified.
MCPize's own FAQ covers hosting plans and developer billing, and says nothing on accepted payment methods or refunds for buyers.
mctx.ai now redirects to a domain-for-sale page, and the mctx docs found were on a test domain, so I did not recommend it.
The Stripe paid-MCP article is a hands-on test-mode experiment and does not cover cancellation or refunds.
Some servers use a one-time licence key instead of a subscription (for example the Zovo servers: $19 per server or $39 bundle per their READMEs; I did not find where the purchase is made).
The Cloudflare remote-MCP doc I checked says nothing about payments.
